complete.outcome: Built on worktree/backbone as 7a1798d47: List.render(){ return Object.hasOwn(List, "View") ? new List.View({ subject: this, open: 1 }) : undefined; }. One change from your proposal: Object.hasOwn, because a static View on Item (the icon view) would otherwise be inherited by List and built with the wrong args. Wire it from the browser as List.View = <your view class>. Your Item.js views getter/setter merges cleanly with mine only if it stays beside `get view()`: I changed get(), set_one(), lists(), find(), replay_line() and added member(), adopt_slot(), Item.dots, Item.clock, Item.old_hops, Item.generation; I did not touch the view getter.

`core/Item/doc/architecture.md:93` still describes the old line shape: "then `{"k":{"set":…}}`". Since this branch the line is `{"kids":{"k":{"set":…}}}`, and line 97 of the same file now contradicts line 93.

`core/Item/doc/next.md:3` still briefs `set(prop, item)` adoption as unbuilt ("the child is never adopted… keep the known-gap assertions"). This branch built it and flipped those tests, so mark the brief done or move it aside.

The wire changed but its doc didn't: `Tail.js` `send()` now passes `jsonl(path, lines, offset, from, ends)`, and `public/framework/dev/Socket/doc/wire.md:125` still documents only `lines` and `offset`. Add `from` and `ends`, and what `live.js` does with them, plus the old-server fallback.

`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Tail.test.mjs` is a new test that no readme lists. There is no SocketServer readme, `Server/readme.md` doesn't mention it, and wire.md doesn't either. Index it next to the wire doc (law 10).

`List.find` now trusts its Map. A caller that changes `list.items` in place (push, splice, sort) without going through a List verb would make `find()` return `undefined` for a member that exists (`List.js` find: "hit undefined and no unkeyed, so return undefined"). A grep of the worktree found no such caller outside List.js. A one-line warning at `get items()` would protect the next caller.

`Item.set_one` now splits any new dotted key into a path (`Item.js` set_one, first lines), and `Item.dots` does the same for every Task and Session line. So a data field whose name has a dot (`"readme.md"`, `"v1.2"`) can no longer be stored flat. No real file was affected (replay-compare showed no difference), but nothing documents the limit.

The `lists()` cache is checked by how many own keys the item has (`Item.js` lists()). An existing List, already owned by the item, that replaces a non-list field keeps the same count and is missed. This is rare, but a version counter on assignment would be exact.

The brief's proof lines are met with caveats, all of them logged in session.jsonl. The voice session v-sq8y7db replays in 199 ms against a 200 ms bar, from one run. The suite is 118/120: PromptLines and layers fail on the base too. smoke fails the core/Item doc pages and ai2 with the same 6 warnings as michael/dev. The landing line should state these, not "passes".

The replay comparison is described only in the task log, as prose: 5083 files, all identical once the by/ts stamps are left out. The digest files were left in %TEMP%. Committing the two digest .jsonl files, or the `--compare` output, beside `replay-compare.mjs` would let a fresh agent check the claim without rerunning it.

SessionTasks applies only new lines for record-shape sessions (tabs and voice). A spawned agent's task-shape record is still replayed whole on every batch (`SessionTasks.js` read). The readme says so, but brief 1a asked for "applies new lines only" without that limit, so the gap should be filed as a follow-up task.

Old id-only hops warn only in node, and only once per process (`Item.js` set_one, key `member-hop`). The browser counts them in `Item.old_hops` without warning, which differs from the brief's "with a warning"; the task log gives the reason. The comment says "the item tool can report them", but no tool reads `Item.old_hops` yet. Docs still teach the id-only form, which now warns in the item tool: `core/Item/readme.md:81` and `architecture.md:121-122` (`{"<id>":{"move":…}}`).

`delta-flow.test.mjs` runs a demo inside a task folder (`core/Session/tasks/data-shapes/seats/delta-flow/demo-delta-flow.mjs`) and passes when that demo prints "STALE". If the seat folder is archived or the demo's text changes, a core test breaks. The seat's notes still list B2–B10 as open.

Small things in `Item.js`: `static get clock` and `static set clock` are split by `static dots` between them. `find()`'s index misses an item whose id changed to the queried id (only a stale hit is detected).
